note: THE-364 — EIGHT BACKLOG CARDS, bundled because none touches another's files. TWO shipped code, THREE were investigations that correctly end in none, and THREE are split out. (1) THE-107, THE ONLY SECURITY-SHAPED ITEM. `isSuperAdmin()` in firestore.rules accepts EITHER the `superAdmin` custom claim OR `tokenEmail()` against a frozen two-address list, and the email leg is the ROOT of the authority rather than a fallback behind the claim: `set-custom-claims.ts` MINTS the claim FROM that list, so a listed owner for whom setCustomClaims has never run carries no claim at all and the email is the only thing identifying them. NOTHING ON ANY SURFACE CHECKS `email_verified` — not the rules, not `verifyAuth`, not `functions/src/index.ts` — and `AuthPage` does not screen the address at signup, so the exposure is precisely: any listed address with no Firebase Auth account yet is claimable by anyone, unverified, and is instantly a full platform owner on all three surfaces. Firebase's one-account-per-email setting is the only thing closing it, and only for an address that is already registered. REPORTED WITH THE EXACT REPLACEMENT RULE AND NOT APPLIED: firestore.rules auto-deploys on merge with no emulator tests, THE-313's one line turned 46 files red, and whether the founder's own Auth records are verified decides whether the fix locks them out. WHAT WAS FIXED IS THE CLIENT CHECK: Profile.tsx tested `isSuperAdminEmail(data.email)` against the user's OWN users doc, and `email` is NOT among the fields the self-edit rule fences, so it was attacker-writable. It was never an escalation — the rules read `request.auth.token.email`, which no client can write — so the forged field opened a door onto a room where every read is still denied; it is fixed because a client that disagrees with the boundary is a false alarm and a support ticket. (2) THE-218 CONFIRMED AND FIXED AT THE SEED. `scripts/seed-platform-tenant.js` wrote `plan: 'ministry'` — the DISPLAY NAME of the `max` tier, where a TenantPlan ID belongs — so getPlanFeatures, getPlanLimits and toTenantPlan all fell through to their unknown-plan default, which is INDIVIDUAL, and Harvest's own tenant ran on the caps of a $49 church. Fixed to `plan: 'max'` AT THE SEED and not at read time: a resolver taught that 'ministry' means 'max' would leave the other two wrong and add a cell nothing else honours, which is the defect plan-features.ts records three deleted cells for. The script must be DISPATCHED AGAIN for the fix to reach production. (3) THE-171 ANSWERED, NOT CHANGED: Dodo does emit `subscription.cancelled`, the handler routes it and `subscription.expired` to real, distinct handlers, and a cancellation archives the tenant immediately — which is also the answer to 86bbnjmx8, since Dodo's portal already offers cancel-at-period-end. Drift found beside it and pinned rather than closed: `subscription.past_due` and `subscription.unpaused` are documented today and unrecognised. (4) THE-101 is a console action; the suite establishes that every month doc carries `expiresAt` and that the persistent `usage/ingest` stock carries none, so the sweep can never reach a live counter. (5) THE-52 SHIPS NO CAP: community messages are TEXT ONLY — an attachment is a reference to an existing doc/contact/campaign/form, no Storage object exists on this path — the feature is Ministry-only with no paying churches, and the only binding enforcement point is firestore.rules. (6) THE-98 and (7) THE-56 are SPLIT OUT; THE-56 is a different repository besides. (8) THE-43 NOT BUILT: a general-purpose composer to every church is marketing-capable by construction and `transactional-email.ts` carries no unsubscribe, postal address or suppression check. EVERY GUARD WAS VERIFIED BY MUTATION — eighteen of them, including weakening requireSuperAdmin to isAdmin, dropping the email leg, reverting Profile.tsx, special-casing the platform tenant, reverting the seed, shrinking the TTL, enrolling the ingest stock in it, unrouting subscription.cancelled, and editing each of the four frozen paths — and every one failed before being reverted.

entries.why: THE-364 owns this APPEND and nothing else in the file, exactly as THE-362 owned the one before it and THE-361 the one before that. `RULES_PINNERS_NOW` goes 75 -> 76 and this bundle's guard suite joins `RULES_PINNERS_ADDED_SINCE` beside THE-362's entry, never over it — the documented cost of adding a suite that pins firestore.rules through the shared register. No accepted value is widened, no pinner is retired and the exact floor still may not shrink. THE-364 RECORDS NO firestore.rules DIGEST ANYWHERE, and for this bundle that is the headline rather than an omission: TWO of its eight cards landed on a rule and both stopped at the file. THE-107 found that `isSuperAdmin()` accepts `tokenEmail()` with no `email_verified` test on any surface, which makes an unregistered super-admin address claimable by anyone; the replacement rule is one line and is written out in the pull request rather than applied, because whether the founder's own Auth records are verified decides whether it locks the platform owner out, and no test here can read that. THE-52 was asked for a message cap on Community Groups, and a cap is only a cap where it BINDS — this file — so the number and the rule text are reported and nothing ships. The rule is ASSERTED as it stands through `rulesDigestFailure()` rather than spelled as a literal, which is the mistake this register caught #504 making, and the four frozen paths were each mutated to prove the assertion is not vacuous.
